entities.name: Julius the Veteran
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Julius the Veteran, a Christian martyr venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church, Roman Catholic Church, and the Church of England, was born in Durostorum (modern-day Istanbul, Turkey) around 250 CE. As a soldier, he served in the Roman Empire, fighting in the Eastern Roman Empire's wars against the Persians and Germanic tribes. Julius's early Christian beliefs led to his arrest and execution by beheading on May 27, 304 CE, in Durostorum.

His legacy as a martyr and saint has had a lasting impact on Christian theology and practice, particularly in the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic traditions. The feast day of Saint Julius the Veteran is celebrated on May 27, and he is revered as a patron saint of soldiers, sailors, and people in danger.

In the 5th century, the Byzantine Empire officially recognized Julius as a saint, and his relics were placed in the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople (modern-day Istanbul). The saint's cult spread throughout the Eastern Roman Empire, and he became a popular subject in Byzantine art and literature.
